simple.meaning: סׇלְעָם (çolʻâm) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a kind of locust (from its destructiveness).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Leviticus, beginning at Leviticus 11:22. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סׇלְעָם (H5556) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: סׇלְעָם (çolʻâm) / H5556 is traced through Leviticus 11:22 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: a kind of locust (from its destructiveness)
definitions.full: H5556. solam סָלְעָם noun masculine an edible, winged, locust (Late Hebrew id.; swallower, consumer , compare סַלְעֵם ᵑ7 swallow up, destroy ; Arabic verb swallow , Kö ii. 1, 404 ); — Lev 11:22 (+ חַגָב חַרְגֹּל, אַרְבֶּה, ).
definitions.rootNote: apparently from the same as 5553 in the sense of crushing as with a rock, i.e. consuming;

occurrences.englishText: Even of these you may eat: any kind of locust, any kind of katydid, any kind of cricket, and any kind of grasshopper.
